# `armadad endpoint`

<!-- Generated by `make docs` from the commands; do not edit. -->

[All commands](armadad.md)

A machine's endpoint is the public IPv4 address WireGuard packets from nodes in
other sites, or from every node in a mesh cluster, are sent to (ADR 0049, ADR
0050). Without one set, a node announces the only public IPv4 address on its
interfaces. Set it behind one-to-one NAT (the public address is on no
interface), on a machine with several, or when its address changed for good.

`set none` says the machine is behind NAT: it has no address others reach, and
it starts every connection to other sites; nodes behind NAT in two sites reach
each other through a relay (ADR 0050). Servers need an endpoint.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`armadad endpoint set`](#armadad-endpoint-set) | Set the endpoint and restart this machine's Armada service |
| [`armadad endpoint show`](#armadad-endpoint-show) | Show the endpoint this machine announces |

## `armadad endpoint set`

Set the endpoint and restart this machine's Armada service.

```
armadad endpoint set IP|none [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
sudo armadad endpoint set 203.0.113.7    # the public address other sites reach this machine at
sudo armadad endpoint set none           # behind NAT
```

Flags:

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--no-restart` | only record the endpoint; restart the service yourself |

## `armadad endpoint show`

Show the endpoint this machine announces.

```
armadad endpoint show
```

Examples:

```bash
sudo armadad endpoint show
```
